subject: Feasibility: isolated-hosting resourcing and architecture clarifications
messages:
From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acme-corp.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Isolated hosting feasibility — initial ask

Hi Mateo / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're moving toward a procurement decision and need a short feasibility read so our security and network teams can sign off. High-level asks: 

- Can Redwood run a VPC-restricted/isolated deployment inside our AWS account with no public egress?
- We will likely require KMS/HSM integration for key custody and an air-gap option for a subset of traffic.
- Expected operational SLA, on-call ownership split, and estimated FTE to support a GA-like install (not a POC) — specifically, ops + infra hours per month.

Our timeline is tight — procurement wants a short document and an ops contact by end of next week. Attaching our internal network requirements and the procurement intake form (see attachments).

Can you confirm what you need from us to evaluate this and a rough estimate of people/time?

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Jenkins
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Corp

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Isolated hosting feasibility — initial ask

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Priyom (platform) and Monica (CS) so we can assemble a short feasibility summary. Quick clarifications from us before we commit: 

- "No public egress": do you mean absolutely zero outbound internet, or allow controlled outbound to specific endpoints (e.g., Redwoods' control plane endpoints for metrics/fallback)?
- For KMS/HSM: do you have a preferred HSM vendor (AWS CloudHSM vs customer HSM appliance) and are you expecting Redwood-managed keys or customer-managed keys?
- Air-gap subset: is the requirement that some components be fully air-gapped (no network to Redwoods) or that data planes are isolated with occasional offline bundle updates?

Action: Priyom, can you draft a short ops/arch note that maps to Sam's checklist (network, keys, oncall, FTE)? Monica, can you add procurement contacts and any billing constraints?

I'll aim to send a one-page feasibility note by EOD tomorrow for procurement, with an attached high-level cost delta.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acme-corp.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-22T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Isolated hosting feasibility — initial ask

Hi Sam — adding the procurement details you asked for. Attached: SOC2_summary.pdf (short), network_diagram_v1.png (your team's sketch annotated), and our current cost_estimate_q3.xlsx (rough delta estimates from hosted to isolated). Points for procurement: 

- Billing model: We can do a reserved-capacity contract (monthly invoice) or a hybrid contract that separates platform fee + infra pass-through. Procurement usually prefers a single invoice line item for committed capacity.
- Contract exceptions: Acme will need a limited SLA exception clause for islands/air-gapped installs; legal will want to see audit log retention and encryption-at-rest/in-transit language.
- Timeline ask: If we move quickly, initial scoping and an architecture decision could be done in 2–3 weeks; delivery to GA depends on resourcing and approvals.

Sam — looping in a short list of required items from your side so we can finalize the note to procurement: VPC CIDR allocation, preferred KMS/HSM approach, list of allowed egress endpoints (if any), and whether your security team requires signed FIPS modules. If you can share those by EOD Friday we can include them in the procurement package.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2028-08-22T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Isolated hosting feasibility — initial ask

Hi all — technical read from platform/infra perspective. Short answers up front, details below.

Summary (tl;dr):
- VPC-restricted deployment with zero public egress is feasible but requires a hardened control plane pattern or an offline bundle mechanism. Expect a 4–6 week engineering effort for a GA-grade integration, plus ongoing 0.5–1.5 FTE ops depending on traffic profile.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed KMS keys in AWS (CloudKMS/AWS KMS) and can integrate with CloudHSM for tenant-owned HSM when needed. Full FIPS-validated HSM appliances for on-prem will add additional compliance work.
- Air-gap: fully air-gapped runtime nodes are possible; practical approach is to ship signed runtime bundles and use an out-of-band signing pipeline to validate images. That reduces network complexity but increases release cadence friction.

Technical notes:
1) Network:
   - For strict zero-egress, we propose a private control plane mirror running inside the customer VPC that accepts signed job manifests. That mirror will need periodic bundle sync via an approved offline process or an allowed egress gateway.
   - Peering or PrivateLink is preferred; transit through an approved NAT is a last resort.
2) Ops/oncall:
   - For GA, platform recommends: 0.5 FTE SRE (on-call rotation) + 0.5 FTE infra engineer for first 3 months for onboarding. If Acme expects high-throughput (sustained RPS), add 1.0 FTE for capacity ops.
3) Security/compliance:
   - Audit logs can be stored in the customer's logging account; Redwood will forward signed, tamper-evident bundles. Retention and access controls are configurable.
4) Cost:
   - Rough delta estimate attached. Major drivers: separate control plane hosting, dedicated instances (reserved pricing), and engineering onboarding hours.

Open questions for Acme (impact timeline):
- Is Acme able to host a small control-plane mirror in their VPC (recommended)? Yes/no.
- Will Acme manage key lifecycle in their KMS or want Redwood to rotate keys on their behalf?

I can draft a 1-page architecture summary for procurement that we can attach to the RFP. If you want, we can also prepare a triage runbook that maps failure modes to on-call actions.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Staff Engineer, Platform — Redwood Inference

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-23T15:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Isolated hosting feasibility — initial ask

Sam — thanks for the quick response and for sharing the procurement materials. Attached below is the plan I'm sending to procurement (short, actionable):

1) Scope we can support (short): VPC-isolated runtime with customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS/CloudHSM), optional offline bundle update path for air-gapped nodes, and audit log forwarding to customer logging account.
2) Resource ask (estimated): 0.5 FTE SRE (ongoing), 0.5 FTE infra for onboarding (first 3 months), 1 platform engineer for initial integration (4–6 weeks), and monthly joint runbook reviews (0.1 FTE).
3) Architecture constraints: requires either PrivateLink/Peering or a customer-hosted control-plane mirror; zero public egress will increase maintenance windows for updates.
4) Contract/billing: prefer reserved capacity + platform fee. Will provide a cost estimate line item for procurement.

Next steps / action items: 
- Sam: confirm whether Acme can host a small control-plane mirror in the VPC or whether you require entirely offline bundle delivery (answer by 2028-08-25).
- Acme security: share KMS/HSM preferences and list of allowed egress endpoints (if any) by 2028-08-25.
- Redwood: Priyom to produce 1-page architecture summary and a concise ops-oncall matrix by 2028-08-24.
- Redwood: Monica to attach cost_estimate_q3.xlsx and bill model summary to the procurement packet.

If that timeline looks good, Monica and I will post the procurement packet to the shared drive and follow up with a 30-minute sync this week to walk security through the architecture.

Thanks — appreciate the fast cadence.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments: SOC2_summary.pdf, network_diagram_v1.png, cost_estimate_q3.xlsx
